{{Quote|Journey to The Edge of the Galaxy''"<br />"''The Closest Thing to Heaven|An advertisement for the Family Adventure Package on Tourscan|<ref name="Star Tours" />}}
'''The Edge of the Galaxy''' was a [[Star system/Legends|star system]] located in the [[Braxant sector/Legends|Braxant sector]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="EAOC" /> By the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[4 ABY/Legends|4.3 ABY]],<ref name="KOTHB">{{Blog|holocron|7|Death Star timeline}}</ref> it was home to a new and exotic resort that included the [[Rodon Value Pod Hotel]], the [[Solar Power Plant]], and the [[Space Observatory]], as well as an [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] installation. The [[Star Tours/Legends|Star Tours]] travel agency facilitated transit to The Edge of the Galaxy resort through their [[Family Adventure Package]].<ref name="Star Tours" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Edge of the Galaxy first appeared in an advertisement on [[Tourscan]] at the [[Tokyo Disneyland]] [[Star Tours (real-world)|''Star Tours'']] attraction,<ref name="Star Tours" /> which opened on [[July 12]], [[1989]].<ref name="TokyoDate">{{ThisWeek|EU-glArwz-U|The Bad Batch Returns, Your Photos of The Child, and More!|sw_url=video/the-bad-batch-returns-your-photos-of-the-child-and-more}}</ref> The [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|Online Companion]] to the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the system in grid square K-3.<ref name="EAOC" />

The location and footage were reused from the Brava Centauri ending segment from [[Wikipedia:Horizons (Epcot)|Horizons]], a now-defunct [[Wikipedia:Epcot|Epcot]] ride, which focused on the concept of [[Wikipedia:Space colonization|space colonization]]. The models for Horizons' three ending segments were designed, constructed, and filmed by [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] special effects veteran [[David Jones]]. The [[Wikipedia:Outer space|space]] sequence was created with input from [[Wikipedia:Princeton University|Princeton]] [[Wikipedia:Physicist|physicist]] [[Wikipedia:Gerard K. O'Neill|Gerald K. O'Neill]] and the [[Wikipedia:Jet Propulsion Laboratory|Jet Propulsion Laboratory]] was consulted regarding growing [[Wikipedia:Crystal|crystals]] for [[Wikipedia:Semiconductor|semiconductors]] in space.<ref name="Epcot">{{WebCite|url=http://progresscityusa.com/2011/09/01/the-horizons-story-part-iii-disneys-house-of-magic|text=The Horizons Story, Part III: Disney's House Of Magic|author=Michael Crawford|date=2011-09-24|work=The Horizons Story|archivedate=20110924203238}}</ref> Model maker Kenneth A. Larson started making all the large parts and turnings on a machine [[Wikipedia:Lathe|lathe]], though assembly of the Brava Centauri sequence was delayed until [[Wikipedia:Neon lighting#Neon tube lighting and signs|neon tubes]] could be completed. By the time they were ready, Larson had already moved on to the [[Wikipedia:Mesa Verde|Mesa Verde]] sequence and Dave Heilman completed the assembly and detailing.<ref name="Horizons Pavilion">{{WebCite|url=http://www.kesigndesign.com/code/horizon1.shtml|text=Choose Your Tomorrow attraction, Horizon Pavilion, EPCOT, Walt Disney World Visual Effects - Model and Prop Builder and Special Effects.|author=Kenneth A. Larson|archivedate=20140327071735}}</ref>
